howto.name: Meet the basic requirements
howto.text: Be at least 18 with a high school diploma or equivalent and a U.S. Social Security number.

howto.name: Complete the 63-hour pre-license course
howto.text: Finish Florida's state-approved 63-hour sales associate pre-license course and pass its end-of-course exam.

howto.name: Get fingerprinted
howto.text: Submit electronic fingerprints through a state-approved vendor for your background check.

howto.name: Apply to the DBPR
howto.text: Apply to the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation and receive your exam authorization.

howto.name: Pass the Florida state exam
howto.text: Pass the 100-question Florida sales associate exam (75% or higher) at a Pearson VUE testing center.

howto.name: Activate your license under a broker
howto.text: Join a licensed Florida broker, such as Adams, Cameron & Co., to activate your license and start working.

Edgewater is a growing city of about 25,000 in southeast Volusia County, sitting along the Indian River and Mosquito Lagoon between New Smyrna Beach to the north and Oak Hill to the south. It’s known as a more affordable, family-friendly alternative to the beachside towns close by, with real waterfront access on the Indian River side even though it isn’t directly oceanfront. Here's exactly how to get licensed, and what the local market looks like for a new agent.

How do you get a real estate license in Edgewater?

You earn the Florida real estate sales associate license, valid statewide. There is no separate Edgewater license. Be 18+ with a high school diploma, complete the 63-hour pre-license course, get fingerprinted, apply to the DBPR, pass the state exam (75% to pass), and activate under a broker. Most people finish in two to four months. Full detail is in our Florida licensing guide.

Is Edgewater a good market for a new real estate agent?

Yes, especially for an agent who wants to work with buyers looking for value and space rather than beachfront price tags. Edgewater draws first-time buyers, growing families, and retirees who want real Indian River and Mosquito Lagoon waterfront access, boating, fishing, and kayaking, without paying New Smyrna Beach prices. Across Volusia County, about 900 homes sell each month at a $343,000 median, and Edgewater’s relative affordability compared to its coastal neighbors keeps steady demand flowing from buyers priced out of the beach.

Boston Whaler and Edgewater’s boating heritage: a real economic anchor

In 1993, Boston Whaler, the iconic fiberglass boat manufacturer, moved all of its manufacturing operations from Massachusetts to Edgewater. That single decision anchored a culture of boating, fishing, and waterfront expertise that runs deep in the community. For an agent, this isn’t just trivia. Edgewater buyers include people drawn to the area specifically for boating, fishery workers, suppliers and employees in the marine trades, and retirees who spent careers in maritime work. They talk watercraft and water access differently than a generic suburban buyer. Understanding who Boston Whaler brought to Edgewater, and why people stay, opens a whole market segment many agents in newer subdivisions never encounter.

The Indian River and Mosquito Lagoon: waterfront real estate at a different price

Edgewater is the heart of the region’s blueway system, a scenic network of water trails for kayaking, paddleboarding, and boating that attracts adventure-oriented families and retirees planning active retirement. Menard-May Park, Kennedy Point Memorial Park, Veterans Park, and Indian River Lagoon Park provide free or low-cost public boat ramps, fishing piers, and direct access to two of Florida’s richest fishing waters. The Mosquito Lagoon and Indian River support year-round fishing for redfish, tarpon, speckled trout, snook, mangrove snapper, and black drum. Over 150 acres of parks and an extensive riverside walk along the Intracoastal Waterway give the town a genuine waterfront lifestyle. What matters for agents: buyers willing to pay for waterfront property but not oceanfront prices find real options here that don’t exist two miles north in New Smyrna Beach, and the public water access keeps property values from purely private luxury pricing.

Edgewater’s waterfront edge: why being on the lagoon, not the ocean, matters

Edgewater took its name from sitting on the edge of the Mosquito Lagoon when the city was renamed in 1924. That geography is the whole story for real estate. Waterfront homes here cost substantially less than oceanfront properties on the nearby coast, yet buyers get genuine Indian River and lagoon access, established parks, natural habitat, and stable demand. The lagoon is protected, shallow in places, and perfect for kayaking and smaller fishing boats. Agents working here discover a buyer profile that doesn’t exist in ocean-view markets: retirees and second-home buyers who specifically want to avoid ocean-facing storm exposure and maintenance, families who value calm-water recreation over waves, and boaters who prefer the lagoon ecosystem. That’s a pricing advantage and a different sales conversation from the coastline.

Edgewater’s aging, owner-occupied base: a stable, long-term market

Edgewater has a median age of 53.7 years and an owner-occupancy rate of 90.1%, one of the highest in the county. That means the market is built on people who buy and stay, not investment properties or rapid turnover. Single-family detached homes make up over 80% of the housing stock, creating a neighborhood feel rather than a transient rental culture. For new agents, this translates into solid repeat and referral potential: owners who have lived in their homes for years know their neighbors, care about the community, and are likely to recommend an agent who serves them well. The demographic skew toward established homeowners also means less price volatility and more predictable seasonality than beach tourist markets.

Does the brokerage you start with matter?

More than the town you pick. Your license must be held by a broker, and that brokerage decides your training, tools, and support in the make-or-break first year. A recognized local name carries real weight. Sellers trust it before you say a word.

Why start your real estate career with Adams, Cameron & Co.?

Adams, Cameron & Co. has been the area's largest brokerage since 1963, with around 300 agents and offices in Port Orange and Daytona Beach serving the Edgewater market. New agents get in-house marketing at no cost, seven-day non-competing manager support, structured training, and the global Leading Real Estate Companies of the World referral network, the credibility that matters when you're building a reputation in a growing, value-conscious market.

What is your next step?

Read the licensing guide, see the neighborhoods worth knowing in our Edgewater neighborhood guide, go deeper on the town’s real story in our full history of Edgewater, then start a conversation with Adams, Cameron & Co. No pressure, just a clear picture of the path.
